To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Sun has a metallicity of [Fe/H] = 0:00 ± 0:02 (i.e. the solar iron abundance log e = 8:52 ± 0:01) when using the full 3.5D model; the Sun has an overall metallicity of [M/H] = 8.43 ± 0.03 when using the full (3.5)D model.
the solar abundances of Na, Mg, Si and S are 6.21, 7.59, 6.43 and 7.51 (dex), and the solar abundance of Ca and Ti are 6.32 and 6.03 (dex), all with an uncertainty of 0.04 (dex).

the solar Na abundance is log e = 4.99 ± 0.03, the solar Mg abundance is log e 6.41 ± 0.04, the solar Al abundance is log e < 6.30, the solar Si abundance is log e > 7.45 and the solar Ca abundance is log e ~ 6.32 ± 0.02.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the most accurate determination possible of the solar chemical composition, which is an essential reference for astrophysics, and the most important star in our Galaxy.
providing a comprehensive and self-consistent picture of the solar chemical composition, with the aim of providing a benchmark for future work on solar and stellar spectroscopy.

the most accurate and homogeneous determination of the solar composition, with the aim to serve as a reference for the chemical analysis of other stars, the solar system, the interstellar medium, the Milky Way and other galaxies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have now reached the level of accuracy where the remaining systematic errors are comparable to the statistical ones.
the solar photospheric composition of the Sun as determined from the 3D hydrodynamical model is in very good agreement with the meteoritic values.

the solar photospheric abundances of Na to Ca are 6:2 ± 0:1, 7:6 ± 0:2, 6:4 ± 0:3, 7:5 ± 0:4, 5:4 ± 1:0, 7:1 ± 0:5 and 6:3 ± 0:7, respectively, in terms of the number density relative to hydrogen, with a solar photospheric metallicity
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we recommend the use of the 3d model for solar abundances, but the 〈3D› model for the solar chemical composition.
the solar photosphere is not a 1D, hydrostatic, plane-parallel object, but a highly dynamic, complex, three-dimensional entity.
the solar photosphere is indeed very close to local thermodynamic equilibrium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the solar abundances of the intermediate-mass species are not affected by the controversial 3D effects.
, in the case of intermediate-mass elements, the solar abundances are not significantly affected by departures from LTE, but are strongly dependent on the choice of model atmosphere.
1D model atmospheres, and even the 〈3D› model, do not provide an adequate description of the solar atmosphere, and that the 3D+LTE abundances of all elements are systematically too large.
